correctness.fix: scan_links.py:300. A full-width page break now uses the key (project, "primary", edition), so it shares page state with the primary column next to it. In the reported failure, the Hebrew-only Psalm 91 repeat and Psalm 136:25 sit inside the Hebrew project's transclusion, and the paired primary column has the same project, so their keys match. Their repeated n55/n59 arrows are now suppressed.
correctness.parallel_column_independence: Kept. Columns still use their own role, so the "parallel"/"secondary" keys stay separate. Project still comes from the column first, then the enclosing transclusion. Edition is still part of the key. test_parallel_columns_have_independent_page_states, test_project_columns_and_shared_wrapper_do_not_share_page_state and test_editions_keep_independent_page_states cover this, and none of them depend on the changed line.
correctness.conditional_and_rubric_merging: Unchanged and still correct. Merging takes the union of before/after states per key, and a key that is missing counts as {None}. Sharing one key between full-width text and the primary column means fewer keys, not different merge behaviour. A full-width page change inside a conditional or rubric gives a state like {old, new}, so the next primary link after the scope is never suppressed.
correctness.actual_page_changes_and_return_visits: Kept. A link is suppressed only when the state for that key is exactly {page}. A new page, or a return to an earlier page after a change, still links. The page is identified by its facs URL, not its n label.
correctness.genuine_first_link: Kept. A key's first appearance has no state, so the link stays. The new key sharing can only suppress a full-width link whose project, edition and scan URL match a primary-column link the reader passes on every path, and the reader has already seen that link. The fix also closes an earlier link-loss bug. Before the fix, a full-width page change inside a conditional did not update the primary state, so a required return to the earlier page was wrongly suppressed. test_conditional_full_width_page_change_preserves_required_primary_link shows this: the old code produced ['1','2'] instead of ['1','2','1'].

findings.issue: A <p:parallelItem> that has no @role still gets role None. That is now a different stream from full-width text ("primary"). If the compiler can emit role-less items, duplicate arrows could come back there. Suggestion: `role = (column.get('role') if column is not None else None) or 'primary'`, if role-less items count as the primary column.

Full-width text gets its project from the nearest transclusion. If that transclusion's p:project is not the primary column's p:project (for example, a book-level wrapper project), the keys still differ and duplicate arrows remain. The error goes towards an extra arrow, never a lost one. Full-width text in the translation project gets the key (en, primary, ed), separate from the English (en, parallel, ed) column. Again this gives possible duplicates, not losses.

Already there before this fix: `if __name__ == '__main__': unittest.main()` sits before several test classes, so running the file directly as a script skips TestStayingInItsOwnText and later classes, including TestPageChanges. pytest is not affected.
Optional: the docstring could say that full-width text continues the primary column's page stream.
